Russian Geology and Geophysics 59 (2018) 276–284

The Campanian–Maastrichtian magnetostratigraphy of the Volga region
(vicinity of Volsk town)
A.A. Guzhikova a,*, V.N. Ben’yamovskii b,†
a N.G. Chernyshevsky Saratov National Research University, Astrakhanskaya ul. 83, Saratov, 410012, Russia
b Geological Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences, Pyzhevsky per. 7, Moscow, 119017, Russia
Received 22 August 2016; accepted 1 September 2016
Abstract
Paleomagnetism and rock magnetism have been studied for the first time in Campanian–Maastrichtian carbonate deposits (Sengilei, Karsun,
and Radishchev Formations) from the Bolshevik and Kommunar quarries near the town of Volsk (Saratov area, Volga region). Characteristic
components of normal and reverse polarity were detected in samples demagnetized in the alternating field, and positive results of the reversal
test were obtained. The virtual geomagnetic pole wander paths calculated for the Sengilei Formation and lower Karsun Formation rocks
showed statistical similarity to those for stable Europe of the respective age. The magnetostratigraphic zones revealed in the Bolshevik and
Kommunar sections were correlated to chrons 33r, 32n2, 32n1, and 31r of the geomagnetic polarity time scale. The magnetic zones of
predominantly reverse and normal polarity detected, though discontinuously, in the low magnetic uppermost Karsun Formation and in the
Radishchev Formation correspond to the top of chron 31r and joint chrons 31n and 30n, respectively. Rock magnetic data help identifying
deposits rich in cosmogenic metal particles and provide stratigraphic constraints on the Radishchev Formation base.
© 2018, V.S. Sobolev IGM, Siberian Branch of the RAS. Published by Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: paleomagnetism; magnetostratigraphy; Campanian; Maastrichtian; cosmogenic particle; Volga region
